skills.rule: Depth is a bar, not an aspiration. Cover the topic A to Z, and if an expert would ask but what about X, X must be addressed: absolute dates on anything time-sensitive, present-day facts searched rather than recalled, no fabricated statistic, quote or citation. It writes chapters and syncs the one row belonging to the page it just built. The moment the question is about the collection, it is study-librarian.

skills.rule: A library is a graph, not a pile. Every page must be reachable through a category, a prerequisite or a related link; a page with no links in or out is reported as an orphan, and gaps are first-class findings reported beside them. It edits properties, links, stubs and whole pages, and never writes a chapter.

gloss.d: The fixed skeleton in order: meta callout, purpose callout, intro hook, sub-pages index near the top, topic heading, rule, table of contents, chapters, then Glossary, Resources and Sources.
A real H2 heading, never a toggle. It opens on a hook, then the substance is shaped to the material. Never numbered unless a real numeric or priority order exists.
Reserved for minor or appendix content: long tangents, raw data, extended derivations. A page that is a wall of collapsed toggles is wrong.
At the very top: Last Updated, Related Pages, and the page-level level (beginner, intermediate, advanced) and reading time.
Page Purpose, Non-scope, and the one-line signpost legend. It sits above everything the page says.
What this page deliberately does not cover, and where that lives instead. The main defence against two pages growing into the same ground.
Sibling and adjacent pages, each with a one-line note on the relationship and the difference. A link with no note is half a link.
The sub-page cards, placed near the top of a hub. The cards already show the titles, so they are the index; a table repeating them next to them reads as a duplicate.
Placed at the exact spot the visual belongs, carrying what to add, why it helps, and a ready Search Google for query, so the image is found and dropped in one step.
For the four things the app does better than the API: uploading an image, converting a video link into a player, native database charts, a hand-drawn mind map. Used sparingly, and only for these.
One to three high-quality videos as descriptive links, grouped in a short section rather than scattered.
Key idea, Example, Analogy, Insight, Watch out, Open question, Go deeper. Applied as inline bold labels so a reader knows what they are looking at without reading it.
A correct page that reads like a generated template is a failure. Personality lives in framing and selection, never in extra words.
Every hyperlink embedded in descriptive words. Also never a dotted domain in the visible link text: Notion auto-links it and creates a broken double link.
Restructure the layout without touching the text. Blocks, list types, headings, toggles, callouts, columns, tables and whitespace may change; words, punctuation, numbers and URLs may not.
The rule Reformat is built on, and the one place the no-em-dash rule yields: an existing em dash is left alone and flagged, because removing it would change punctuation.
A to Z coverage: definitions, why it matters, how to reason about it, the frameworks, the trade-offs, the edge cases, the state of the art. If an expert would ask but what about X, X is addressed.
Cite where a source adds weight: a quote, a statistic, a price, a regulation, an important or contested claim. Not a footnote per line; the page is a sharp study reference, not a thesis.
Attached to anything time-sensitive: prices, regulations, versions, market figures, leadership, any latest claim. Written into the citation, for example as of May 2026.
Where sources conflict, the page prints Uncertainty: [what is unclear] / Reduce via: [what would resolve it] rather than quietly picking a side.
For theory pages, the chapter index and the intended source list are proposed and confirmed before writing, unless you said autonomous. It prevents depth spent on the wrong structure.

Why and how to think is Theory. How do I do it, step by step is Practice, and links the best official guide rather than rewriting it. How is my system set up right now is Real Setup, and lives outside the study library.
Which pages a page should be read after. It encodes the dependency of the material, not your progress, and Audit checks that it is acyclic.
A number, kept coherent across siblings: no gaps and no collisions within a category or series.

A deliberately empty page: title, meta callout, a one-line purpose, a ## To be written note, with category, scope, reading order and prerequisites already set. The Librarian builds the frame, study-os fills it.
The parent of a set: meta callout, purpose and Non-scope, and a ## Deep dives section that holds the sub-page cards.
Category from the existing options, scope, reading order, a sharp one or two line content description, page URL. Never an invented option value.
Overlap detected by comparing titles, descriptions, categories and chapter headings. A genuine duplicate gets a merge proposal; partial overlap gets a scope split instead.
The alternative to merging: each page keeps its slice, written through the Non-scope and Related lines so the boundary is visible on both pages.
A page with no links in and none out. Reachability through a category, a prerequisite or a related link is the minimum bar.
A topic a complete library on this subject would be expected to have and does not. Judgement over the existing category structure, and a first-class finding rather than an afterthought.

One overview page: categories with their pages in reading order, a Mermaid graph of the prerequisite relations, and explicit lists of orphans and gaps. Held to the same page standards as everything else.
Yours. Read where useful, never changed, not even by Organize. The boundary between the material and the learning is absolute.

Fetch the database, then the collection://<data_source_id> from its data-source tag, and read property names and option values from there. No property name, category option or database ID is ever hardcoded.
The dangerous write. It flags child pages and attachments for deletion unless every one is re-included in the new body. Prefer insert_content and update_content on a populated page.
Checkboxes take __YES__ and __NO__, numbers are real numbers, a property literally named id or url needs the userDefined: prefix, and dates split into start, end and is_datetime fields.
The workhorse, because it renders natively. A diagram that can be Mermaid must be Mermaid, never a text placeholder. Arrows are safe inside the block, unlike in Notion text.
Many hosts block hotlinking, so an external image URL creates a block that renders blank. Default to Mermaid or a generated file plus a slot, and pair any embedded URL with a fallback.
The final gate, run in full before anything is presented: depth, structure, visuals, sources, style, metadata, then a re-fetch to confirm tables, columns, Mermaid and page cards actually rendered.
If a sibling covers part of the topic, record the difference in the Non-scope and Related lines instead of repeating the content.
Any topic, any input, any output, any workspace. A missing property is worked around rather than assumed, and one is added only with your consent.

Never, in any output, in any mode: not in Notion, not in a PDF, not in chat. A comma, a colon, parentheses, or split the sentence. Verbatim quoted text is the only exception, and Reformat leaves existing ones alone.

breaks.h: Writing chapters from the Librarian, or curating the collection from Study OS
breaks.b: The two skills stay predictable because the split is by what gets written, not by where the work happens. Cross it once and neither skill is the source of truth for anything.
The schema is read at runtime from the collection:// data source for a reason. Hardcode a category option or a property name and the skill works in exactly one workspace.
It flags child pages and attachments for deletion unless every single one is re-included in the new body. That is where the mistakes happen, and they are not visible until something is already gone.

breaks.h: Wrapping a chapter in a toggle
breaks.b: Chapters are real H2 headings. Toggles are for tangents, raw data and appendix material, and a page that is a wall of collapsed toggles is unreadable.

breaks.b: Many hosts block hotlinking, so the block is created and renders blank. Mermaid, or a generated file with a visible slot, or nothing.
They are your learning state, not the library's. Neither skill writes them, and Audit does not even flag them.

Chapters are real H2 headings, opening on a hook, with the shape inside following the material. Toggles are for appendix content only.
Absolute dates on anything time-sensitive, and search present-day facts rather than recalling them. Where sources conflict, print the uncertainty rather than picking a side.
Connect the page before you leave it. A category, plus a prerequisite or a related link. A page with neither is an orphan the day it is written.
Run the QA rubric in full, then re-fetch. A page that failed to render is indistinguishable from one that was never written.

a Notion URL or update the page means Notion; PDF, printable or hand this to someone means a document. Default is Notion
Known conflict

this file says chapters are toggle headings and describes every chapter as Summary bullets plus Content. page-architecture.md, writing-standards.md and qa-review.md all require real H2 headings and reject one repeated skeleton. Follow the three, not this one

standards.w: Open it when running Reformat. Text invariance, what may and may not change, and the one place the no-em-dash rule yields to it.
k: Invariance
no word, punctuation mark, number, emoji or URL is added, removed or modified. Only block types and whitespace
Scope
if a selection is present, nothing outside it is touched
Order of work
line breaks and blocks, then bullets and checklists, then headings, then toggles, callouts, columns and tables
Tables
only where the text is already table-like and the mapping is unambiguous. No cell text, capitalization or link changes
The exception
an existing em dash is left in place and flagged, because removing it would change punctuation

standards.w: Open it before presenting anything. The final gate, run in full, then fix what failed and re-fetch to confirm the page rendered.
k: Depth
a key idea and at least one concrete, often numeric, example per chapter; the hard points expanded rather than glossed
Structure
the sub-pages index near the top, chapters as real headings, the shape varying per chapter
Visuals
Mermaid where Mermaid is possible, attribution on any embedded image, a slot where a generated asset belongs
Sources
claims, data, quotes and contested points cited, volatile facts dated, nothing fabricated
Style
zero em dashes outside verbatim quotes: scan and remove. Consistent signposts, bold label before a colon
Final
re-fetch and confirm tables, columns, Mermaid and page cards actually rendered

standards.w: Open it for any Librarian mode. Reading the library, metadata hygiene, the two graph layers, deduplication, the map page, and the scaffolding procedure.
k: Read the library
fetch the database and its data source, enumerate the rows and child pages, then build the picture of titles, metadata and who links to whom
Hygiene
category from existing options, scope, reading order coherent across siblings, a sharp one or two line description, page URL
Two graph layers
the Prerequisites self-relation for ordered dependency, and Related lines with inline page mentions for adjacency
Never change
Status and Next review. They are the user's learning state, out of scope
Dedupe
a merge proposal for a genuine duplicate, a scope split for partial overlap. Confirmation first, child pages and attachments preserved
Scaffold
get the plan, confirm the structure, create the hub plus one empty stub per item with metadata and prerequisites, then hand off to study-os

standards.w: Open it when running Audit. The per-page structure, hygiene and metadata checks, the library-level checks, and the report format. Note that several checks here are defined by the two Study OS standards files, so a Librarian installed on its own does not ship the rules it audits against.
k: Per page
meta and purpose callouts, chapters as real headings, a Sources section where claims appear, consistent signposts
Hygiene
no em dashes outside quotes, no bare URLs or dotted-domain labels, no blank image boxes, no leftover placeholders
Metadata
category, scope, reading order, description, page URL. Status and Next review are neither flagged nor changed
Library level
orphans, duplicates, reading-order gaps and collisions, an acyclic prerequisite graph, hub cards that still resolve, and the obvious topic gaps
The report
blockers first, then should-fix, then nice-to-have, each with the page link and the one-line fix, closing with an offer to run Organize and to hand content gaps to study-os

tags: the core insight, in one or two lines
text is split into subword fragments mapped to integer IDs, then to learned vectors
a concrete, real example or mini-scenario, often numeric
1 token is about 0.75 English words, so a 1,000-word memo is roughly 1,300 tokens
a familiar comparison for an abstract or technical idea. One good analogy saves three paragraphs
a lock and key, a tree, a sealed envelope
a sharp, memorable rule of thumb
a common mistake, risk or misconception
what is unsettled or at the frontier, added for meaty topics
the sources and the deep-dive sub-page
weights: standards bodies, peer-reviewed and industry references
low-quality or SEO-spam pages, and anything recalled rather than checked

title: Study OS: how to use it
sub: Two skills, one Notion database, and one test between them. If the change lands inside a page's chapters it is study-os. If it lands between pages, in the metadata, the links, the index or the stubs, it is study-librarian. Organised by the job you are doing. For everything about one skill open its SKILL.md; for the rules it enforces, open the file under references/ that governs the thing you are about to do.
footer: Study OS · everything about one skill lives in its SKILL.md · the operating rules live in references/ · what a skill needs and returns is in HANDBOOK.md · generated by scripts/explorer/build.py, do not edit by hand

model.h: What every skill here does, whatever it is about

model.lede: One owner per object. A skill needing something it does not own reads the identifier and attaches to it, rather than minting a second one for the same thing.

model.h: Anything describing a set of records is computed
model.lede: A field describing other records diverges within a week when typed by hand, and a hand-filled rollup is noise that looks like signal — worse than an empty field, because nobody knows it is wrong.
Different people arrive with different questions. Nobody should have to read a document written for someone else.
Not a beginner mode. This is what stays true at every size; everything else is an addition a specific question makes necessary.

model.h: What to add, and what triggers it
model.lede: Add a field when the question is asked, not in anticipation. And remove one that stopped being read.

model.h: The same model in any environment
model.lede: The mechanism changes, the rule does not. Pick the one your team already opens — a model living in a tool nobody maintains is dead on arrival.

gloss_lede: Every term this suite uses, in one line, grouped by where it lives. The words are not interchangeable — most confusion comes from treating two of them as the same object.
